The musician

Four decades of performance, distilled into teaching

David Cunliffe is a Grammy-nominated cellist and founding member of the Lincoln Trio — described by The Strad as "sensational" and by Gramophone as "models of vibrancy and control." With the Trio, he has performed at Carnegie's Weill Hall, Alice Tully Hall, the Ravinia Festival, and at the Abraham Lincoln Bicentennial with President Barack Obama.

As a founding member of the Black Oak Ensemble and former member of the Balanescu Quartet, he has performed and recorded internationally across Europe, Asia, and South America.

He holds faculty positions at Northwestern University, Merit School of Music, and New Music School in Chicago.

What I offer

01
Performance

Chamber music, solo recitals, and orchestral work across the US and Europe. Available for engagements, collaborations, and festival appearances.

02
Teaching

Private cello lessons in-person and online worldwide. Welcoming adult beginners, returning players, and serious students.

03
Cordes en Gascogne

A summer chamber music festival in the Gers, southwest France — founded in 2015. Intimate concerts in historic settings, each August.

Biography

David
Cunliffe

The musician

Cellist · Chamber Musician · Educator

David Cunliffe is a Grammy-nominated cellist and founding member of the Lincoln Trio — described by The Strad as "sensational" and by Gramophone as "models of vibrancy and control." With the Trio, he has performed at Carnegie's Weill Hall, Alice Tully Hall, the Ravinia Festival, and at the Abraham Lincoln Bicentennial in Springfield, Illinois, with President Barack Obama.

International engagements have taken the Trio across Europe, Asia, and South America. As a member of the Balanescu Quartet, David recorded and toured extensively — including the soundtrack for the film Angels and Insects and the album Arabian Waltz with oud player Rabih Abou-Khalil.

He has performed as principal cello with the BBC Philharmonic, BBC Scottish Symphony, and Royal Scottish National Orchestra, and collaborated with musicians including Shmuel Ashkenasi, Simon Keenlyside, Alberto Lysy, and Ricardo Morales.

As a founding member of the Black Oak Ensemble — praised for its "fierce eloquence" by The Times — David has championed new and rarely heard music, with recordings reaching #1 on the Billboard Classical Charts.

He holds faculty positions at Northwestern University (Bienen School of Music), Merit School of Music, and New Music School in Chicago.

"Polish gives way to moments of artful recklessness."

Cordes en Gascogne

Each August, David returns to the Gers region of southwest France to lead Cordes en Gascogne — a chamber music festival he founded in 2015. Intimate concerts in historic settings, bringing together international musicians in one of France's most beautiful corners.

The festival reflects a belief that chamber music belongs in living rooms and village halls as much as concert halls.

Private Lessons

Online Cello
Lessons

For adult learners — wherever you are in the world.

The approach

Serious teaching,
without the pressure

I work with adult amateurs returning to the cello after a break, complete beginners who've always wanted to play, and advancing students who want thoughtful, detailed guidance from an active professional.

Lessons are on Zoom and built entirely around you — what you want to play, where you want to go, and how much time you have. There's no standard curriculum, no judgment, and no such thing as being too old or too rusty.

30+
Years performing internationally
Zoom
Online worldwide · no travel needed
All
Levels and ages welcome
Who I teach

You might be a good fit if…

The Returning Player
You played as a child or teenager and life got in the way. You'd like to find your way back — without feeling like you have to start from scratch.
The Beginner
You've always wanted to play but never had the chance. Adults often make faster progress than children because they understand what they're aiming for.
The Advancing Student
You're already playing but want more depth — better technique, more musical understanding, or the perspective of a professional with decades of chamber music experience.
What we cover

Lesson Content

—
Tone & bow techniqueDrawing a beautiful sound from the very first lesson
—

—

—
